rules.title: California security deposit law: one-month cap, 21-day return and deduction limits
rules.requirement: Since July 1, 2024, a landlord may not demand or receive a security deposit (however labeled) of more than one month's rent on top of first month's rent; qualifying small landlords may take up to two months' rent. Within 21 days after you move out, the landlord must return the deposit or what remains of it, with an itemized statement, receipts, and (since April 1, 2025) photos for any deductions. The landlord may not deduct for ordinary wear and tear or preexisting damage, and no deposit may be called nonrefundable.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords); return within 21 days
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental security deposits in California, furnished or unfurnished. The one-month cap applies to security demanded or collected on or after July 1, 2024. Move-in photos are required for tenancies beginning on or after July 1, 2025, and move-out/pre-repair photos since April 1, 2025. Electronic return applies from January 1, 2026 where the tenant paid deposit or rent electronically. A higher-than-standard deposit charged to a service member must be explained in writing and the extra returned within six months (from April 1, 2025). The landlord must give written notice of the tenant's right to a pre-move-out inspection, held no earlier than two weeks before move-out.
rules.exemptions: Small landlord exception to the one-month cap: a natural person (including a family trust) or an LLC whose members are all natural persons, owning no more than two residential rental properties with no more than four units offered for rent in total, may take up to two months' rent, but not from a service member. Advance payment of at least six months' rent is allowed on leases of six months or longer. Receipts are not required if repair and cleaning deductions total $125 or less, unless the tenant asks for them within 14 days. The inspection notice does not apply to terminations under CCP § 1161(2)-(4). Electronic return does not apply if the parties agreed in writing to another method.
rules.penalty: Bad-faith retention or demand: statutory damages of up to twice the security plus actual damages; landlord forfeits any claim to the security for bad-faith noncompliance with the return requirements (§ 1950.5(h), (m)).

exemption_tests.description: Small landlord (natural person, family trust, or LLC with all natural-person members) owning no more than two rental properties with no more than four units total may charge up to two months' rent; not applicable to service-member tenants.

rules.conflict_note: Provisions phased in on different dates: cap July 1, 2024 (AB 12); photos April 1 and July 1, 2025 (AB 2801); service-member refund April 1, 2025; electronic return January 1, 2026 (AB 414). These are amendments, not conflicts.
rules.reason: All candidates describe provisions of Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 (deposit cap, return timeline, deductions, photos, inspection, electronic return, nonrefundable ban), so they merge into one record citing the statute text.
